title: SDK rapid rehearsal: 30min demo & rehearsal scripts
content:
Purpose and scope
- Short, repeatable 30-minute demo and rehearsal script for product/SE/internal demo teams to show off Redwood SDKs (JS/Python/Go) and common fallback flows.
- Designed for minimal setup, deterministic results, and clear failure-mode choreography so rehearsals are reliable.
- Not a full tutorial; this is a rehearsal checklist + script to run a tight demo with timeboxed segments.

Audience
- Solutions Engineers (primary), Developer Advocates, PMs prepping a customer walkthrough, and new eng hires practicing the 1st-run story.

Preflight (10 minutes) — always do these before a live run
- Environment: use the sandbox project (RBW-SANDBOX-1) or local mock runner. Confirm network access to api.redwood-internal.test.
- Credentials: export REDWOOD_API_KEY with the demo key. Confirm by running: curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY\" https://api.redwood-internal.test/v1/models | jq '.[0].id'
- Version pin: use model pinned to 2026-01-08 canary (model id: rwj-canary-20260108) to avoid drift.
- Telemetry: open the demo dashboard (console.redwood.local/dash/demo-rehearsal) to watch request traces.
- Fallback toggles: ensure the routing policy env var is set for the rehearsal (REDWOOD_ROUTE_POLICY=prefer-latency).

30-minute run structure (timeboxed)
- 0:00–01:30 — 30s intro, 1 min outline of what's coming. Keep it high-level.
- 01:30–05:00 — Zero-to-first-response: show a 2-line JS snippet, run it, show streaming output.
- 05:00–12:00 — Feature deep-dive: show embeddings and reranking flow (Python sample), highlight latency and cost numbers in Console.
- 12:00–20:00 — Failure-mode demo: simulate high latency on primary model and show automatic fallback to quantized variant. Show the rollout control.
- 20:00–26:00 — Observability + debugging: open trace for earlier request, inspect token-level latency, show telemetry spike and how to annotate trace.
- 26:00–30:00 — Q&A and next steps: how to get a POC, links to quickstart repo and followup actions.

Minimal demo scripts (copy-paste)
- JS: quick generation (streaming)
  node -e "const r=require('./js-sample'); r.streamGen(\"Write a short product-ized commit message: summarize changes and include a 1-line rationale.\");"
  (Note: js-sample uses @redwood/sdk; ensure node env has REDWOOD_API_KEY.)

- Python: embeddings + rerank (single-file)
  python - <<'PY'
  from redwood import RedwoodClient
  c=RedwoodClient(api_key='${REDWOOD_API_KEY}')
  docs=["How to set up a repo", "Quickstart for local dev", "Deploy checklist"]
  q='quickstart local dev checklist'
  emb=c.embeddings.create(docs)
  qemb=c.embeddings.create([q])[0]
  scores=[(i, c.cosine(qemb, e)) for i,e in enumerate(emb)]
  print(sorted(scores, key=lambda x:-x[1]))
  PY

- CLI fallback test: simulate capacity constraint
  export REDWOOD_FAKE_LATENCY_MS=1200
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood-internal.test/v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY\" -d '{"model":"rwj-canary-20260108","prompt":"Explain graceful degradation in 3 bullets"}'
  (Expected: request routed to rwj-quant-20260108; demo the route in Console -> Rollouts)

Failure modes to rehearse (short checklist)
- Auth failure: expired token; demo with BAD key and show 401 + guidance on rotating keys.
- Model drift: pinned model shows different outputs; rehearse how to rollback via Console -> Rollouts -> rollback to stable.
- High latency: use REDWOOD_FAKE_LATENCY_MS to force fallback and show fallback trace.
- Partial outputs: streaming cutoff; show rehydrate via caching/KV prefix mechanisms.

Observability cues to show (scripts)
- Open the request trace for the slow routing: point out per-step timings (client, routing, kernel execution, tokenization).
- Show token-level cost estimate panel and explain how batching settings would reduce cost.

Rehearsal script (spoken lines, condensed)
- Intro: \"Hi — quick 30-minute demo. We'll show zero-to-first-response, embeddings, graceful fallback, and the Console visibility so you can see how Redwood makes inference predictable.\"
- Running code: \"I'll run this tiny snippet — note the streaming response as tokens arrive, and watch the Console for the same trace.\"
- Fallback: \"Now I'll simulate high latency; watch routing switch to a compatible quantized variant and how the SDK surface shows the fallback event.\"
- Observability: \"Here's the trace — click the kernel timing to see where most time is spent, and we'll annotate a debug message for correlation.\"

Artifacts to point customers/attendees to after demo
- github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-samples (quickstart folder)
- Confluence: 30m SDK Rehearsal (linked in metadata)
- Guide: developer-onramp/redwood-quickstart (Confluence)

Open items / TODOs for DE team (owner: Maya)
- [ ] Add a Go snippet to the repo that mirrors Python embedding example (Evan).
- [ ] Create a 'rehearsal' short-play dashboard with pre-filtered traces (SRE request).
- [ ] Bake a deterministic demo dataset and pin it to the sandbox project to avoid nondeterministic hallucinations.
- [ ] Create a one-click ephemeral sandbox environment for SEs (work with infra).

Notes to self / rough edges observed in last run
- Streaming jitter on local Wi-Fi can produce token burst; recommend wired/demo laptop in conference rooms.
- Some attendees asked for cost-per-1000 tokens sample for pinned canary vs quantized variant — add a small table to the slide deck.
- Example prompts need guardrails for safety; add a quick prompt safety checklist.

Appendix: Quick troubleshooting commands
- Check API key: curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY\" https://api.redwood-internal.test/v1/whoami | jq
- Reset route policy locally: unset REDWOOD_ROUTE_POLICY; export REDWOOD_ROUTE_POLICY=prefer-cost
- Replay trace by request id: curl https://console.redwood.local/api/trace/$REQUEST_ID -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY\"

End of doc — rough draft for team review.

Last rehearsal notes (2026-02-28): practiced with Diego and Priya. Need to shorten fallback demo (was ~8 min) to fit 30m cap.
